record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: What is the exact relationship between projected entangled pair states and quantum cellular automata in two and higher spatial dimensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 2$, and fix a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^p$ attached to each site $x \in \Lambda$. A translation-invariant Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) with physical dimension $p$ and bond dimension $D$ is the family of states obtained as follows: place a maximally entangled pair in $\mathbb{C}^D \otimes \mathbb{C}^D$ on every edge of $\Lambda$, and at each vertex $x$ apply a fixed linear map $A : (\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 2d} \to \mathbb{C}^p$ to the $2d$ incoming virtual indices. A Quantum Cellular Automaton (QCA) on $\Lambda$ with on-site Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^p$ is a $*$-automorphism $\alpha$ of the quasi-local algebra $\mathfrak{A} = \overline{\bigotimes_{x\in\Lambda} M_p(\mathbb{C})}$ that is translation-invariant and strictly local, meaning there exists a finite neighborhood $N \subset \Lambda$ such that $\alpha(\mathcal{O}_x) \subset \bigotimes_{y\in x+N} M_p(\mathbb{C})$ for every single-site observable $\mathcal{O}_x$. Given the state $|\Omega\rangle = \bigotimes_{e} |\phi^+\rangle_e$ on the virtual level, every PEPS can be viewed as the image of $|\Omega\rangle$ under a product of local maps; conversely, every QCA in $d=1$ is known to admit a representation as an injective PEPS, and every injective translation-invariant PEPS in $d=1$ arises (in a precise sense) from a QCA.

Determine the exact relationship between translation-invariant PEPS and QCAs in spatial dimensions $d \geq 2$. Specifically:
(a) Characterize which translation-invariant QCAs on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ can be represented as (or are intertwined by) a translation-invariant PEPS map.
(b) Conversely, characterize which translation-invariant PEPS arise from a QCA structure on the virtual level.
(c) In particular, determine whether the equivalence known in $d=1$ extends, fails, or admits a modified form in $d\geq 2$, and identify the obstructions (e.g., nontrivial higher-dimensional QCA invariants).
artifact.category_tag: Tensor networks and quantum cellular automata
artifact.status_search_result: The precise relationship between PEPS and quantum cellular automata in two and higher spatial dimensions remains an active research topic. While the one-dimensional correspondence (between MPS/MPO and QCA) is well established, no general characterization exists in $d \geq 2$, where new QCA invariants are known to exist and obstruct a direct equivalence. Recent works on PEPS limitations and on higher-dimensional QCAs do not resolve the question.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical open problems in projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems on PEPS including connections with QCA.
status_evidence.claim: The exact PEPS–QCA relationship in higher dimensions is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Projected Entangled Pair States: Fundamental Analytical and Numerical Limitations
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes intrinsic limitations of PEPS in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works identify obstructions in higher-dimensional PEPS but do not characterize their QCA structure.
